records.title: BRCA2 C-terminal clamp restructures RAD51 dimers to bind B-DNA for replication fork stability
records.abstract: Tumor suppressor protein breast cancer susceptibility protein 2 (BRCA2) acts with RAD51 in replication fork protection (FP) and homology-directed DNA-break repair (HDR). Critical for cancer etiology and therapy resistance, the BRCA2 C terminus was thought to stabilize recombinogenic RAD51 after the assembly of ATP-extended RAD51 filaments on single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). Here, the detailed crystal structure of the human BRCA2 C-terminal interaction domain (TR2 interface [TR2i]) complexed with ATP-bound RAD51 prior to DNA binding instead reveals TR2i unexpectedly induces a unique ATP-RAD51 dimer conformation that accommodates nucleation onto double-stranded B-DNA unsuited for HDR initiation. Structural, biochemical, and molecular results with interface-guided mutations uncover TR2i’s FP mechanism. Proline-driven secondary structure stabilizes residue triads and spans the RAD51 dimer, engaging pivotal interactions of RAD51 M210 and BRCA2 S3291/P3292, the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) phosphorylation site that toggles between FP during S phase and HDR in G2. TR2i evidently acts as an allosteric clamp, switching RAD51 from ssDNA to double-stranded and B-DNA binding, enforcing FP over HDR, challenging the current BRCA2-RAD51 dogma.

records.title: Postures communicationnelles des spécialistes en médecine générale dans le dépistage familial du cancer colorectal
records.abstract: Introduction : Les apparentés au premier degré de patients atteints de cancer colorectal (CCR) ou d’adénome avancé avant l’âge de 65 ans (patients index) présentent un risque accru de CCR, mais les lignes directrices relatives au dépistage familial des apparentés par coloscopie sont peu suivies. Cette étude a pour objectif de décrire, d’un point de vue linguistique et sociologique, l’implication de spécialistes en médecine générale auprès des patients (apparentés à risque élevé de cancer colorectal ou patients index) et leur posture communicationnelle dans le cadre du dépistage familial auprès des différents protagonistes (autres médecins, patients index, apparentés). Méthode : Elle s’appuie sur 29 entretiens semi-directifs avec des spécialistes en médecine générale français de patients index et/ou de leurs apparentés réalisés par téléphone. Le corpus entièrement transcrit des entretiens a fait l’objet d’une analyse linguistique à l’aide d’un outil lexicométrique qui permet de déterminer les objets de discours et d’une analyse sociologique thématique. records.title: A Comprehensive Review on Thyroid Management And Therapeutic Potential of Medicinal Plants
records.abstract: Thyroid diseases are widespread endocrine disorders that affect a significant portion of the global population. The pathology associated with specific types or stages of thyroid disease is complex and intricately linked to various biological functions. While the mortality rate associated with thyroid dysfunction is relatively low, it can lead to metabolic and immunological disorders that result in considerable discomfort for affected individuals. Currently, numerous pharmaceutical options are available for managing thyroid disease; however, issues such as drug toxicity and prolonged treatment durations highlight the urgent need for more effective alternatives. Thyroid disorders are among the most prevalent endocrine conditions worldwide, affecting individuals across all age groups and contributing significantly to morbidity and reduced quality of life. Effective thyroid management requires accurate diagnosis, appropriate therapeutic interventions, and long-term monitoring to prevent complications and optimize patient outcomes.

records.title: Water Lily or Camelotte Sign in Pulmonary Hydatid Cyst – An Orphan Disease
records.abstract: A 20 – year – old male without any previous comorbidity presented to pulmonary medicine outpatient department with complaints of dull aching chest pain on right side, dry cough and shortness of breath for the pastone year. He was non vegetarian and had no addictions. On general physical examination his vitals were stableand respiratory system examination revealed decreased breath sounds in the right hemithorax. All his routineblood investigations were normal. Chest radiograph revealed homogenous opacity in the right middle andlower zones. Contrast enhanced computed tomography of thorax and abdomen showed a well defined encapsulatedcystic lesion of size 12x10x14cm with internal floating membranes (water lily sign or Camelotte sign) with masseffect on adjacent lung parenchyma causing atelectasis and compression of adjacent vessels (Figure 1). Hydatid serology (IgG) was positive. Patient was treated symptomatically and referred for surgical intervention.

records.title: Aromatic polyketides from the marine-derived fungus Aspergillus unguis PM03: α-glucosidase inhibitory activity, structure-activity relationship, molecular docking and ADMET evaluation
affiliations: Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology
Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City
Trường Đại học Khoa học Sức khỏe
records.abstract: Chemical investigation of Aspergillus unguis PM03 yielded eight known aromatic polyketides, including unguinol (1), nidulin (2), 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3), 2-chlorounguinol (4), emeguisin B (5), aspergillusether A (6), guisinol (7), and isosclerone (8). Their structures were established by spectroscopic analysis and comparison with published data. All isolated compounds were evaluated for cytotoxicity against four human cancer cell lines (KB, Hep-G2, A549, and MCF-7) and for α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. None of the compounds exhibited significant cytotoxicity (IC50 > 128 μM). Compounds 1, 3, 5, 7, and 8 inhibited α-glucosidase, with guisinol (7) showing the strongest activity (IC50 = 4.01 μM), followed by isosclerone (8) (11.39 μM), emeguisin B (5) (24.31 μM), unguinol (1) (26.28 μM), and 2,4-dichlorounguinol (3) (28.83 μM). To our knowledge, this is the first report of the α-glucosidase inhibitory activity of compounds 1–7. A preliminary structure–activity relationship analysis suggested that the substitution pattern of the aromatic polyketides may affect their inhibitory activity. Molecular docking of compounds 1–7 and four aromatic polyketides previously isolated in our studies was performed against penicillin-binding protein 2a (PBP2a; PDB ID: 1MWT), together with in silico ADMET prediction to assess their pharmacokinetic properties.

records.title: Analysis of blood components and the mechanism of anti-pharyngitis and gut microbiota regulation in Ardisia crenata and its relatives
records.abstract: This study comprehensively integrated network pharmacology, molecular docking, and gut microbiota analysis to explore the anti-pharyngitis targets and pathways of Ardisia crenata Sims (ZSG), Ardisia crenata Sims var.bicolor (Walk) (HLS) and Ardisiacrispa (Thunb.) (BLJ), and to investigate their underlying mechanisms. PPI networks and “herb-component-target-disease” networks were constructed, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analysis. Molecular docking demonstrated strong binding affinity between the active components and the core targets. Additionally, changes in gut microbiota and endogenous metabolites in rats were analyzed by combining 16S rDNA high-throughput sequencing and untargeted metabolomics. The results revealed that the central targets are SRC, TNF, PIK3CA, STAT3, JAK2. KEGG analysis highlighted notable involvement of the PI3K/AKT, Rap1, Ras, Estrogen signaling pathways. Moreover, all three herbs were found to modulate the gut microbiota to some extent, contributing to the alleviation of microbial dysbiosis. In conclusion, ZSG, HLS and BLJ exert anti-pharyngitis effects through multi-target and multi-pathway mechanisms.

records.title: Caracterización clínica y epidemiológica de la bronquitis aguda en pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años durante 2023
records.abstract: Introducción: La bronquitis aguda es una de las infecciones respiratorias más frecuentes en la población pediátrica y representa una causa importante de consulta y hospitalización en América Latina. Metodología: Se realizó un estudio observacional, descriptivo, transversal y retrospectivo mediante revisión de historias clínicas electrónicas de 83 pacientes pediátricos de 2 a 12 años con diagnóstico de bronquitis aguda atendidos durante enero–diciembre de 2023. Resultados: Predominó el sexo masculino (61,4%) y el grupo de 2 a 4 años (44,6%). La tos fue la manifestación más frecuente (92,8%), seguida de fiebre (62,7%) y sibilancias (51,8%). Las complicaciones más frecuentes fueron la exacerbación del asma (10,8%) y la otitis media aguda (8,4%). Los broncodilatadores inhalados fueron el tratamiento más utilizado (75,9%), seguidos de antipiréticos (72,3%); los antibióticos se emplearon en 13,3%. Conclusiones: La bronquitis aguda presentó predominio masculino, mayor frecuencia en niños de 2 a 4 años y una presentación clínica caracterizada principalmente por tos. Las complicaciones graves fueron poco frecuentes y el uso de antibióticos fue limitado.

records.title: Extraction and purification, pharmacological effects, and product development of oridonin: a review
records.abstract: Isodon rubescens (I. rubescens), a plant of the family Lamiaceae, is the dried aerial part of I. rubescens (Hemsl.) Hara. It has the effects of clearing heat and detoxifying, relieving pain, promoting blood circulation, and reducing swelling. As a highly valued traditional Chinese medicine, it contains a variety of chemical components. Among them, oridonin (ORI) exhibits antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer properties, garnering significant attention in pharmacological research. Furthermore, ORI serves as a crucial quality control marker for I. rubescens. It can exert biological effects on the nervous, cardiovascular, and visceral organ systems via multiple signaling pathways, thereby conferring potential therapeutic value for related diseases. To improve the efficacy and safety of its applications and ensure that the isolated monomer compounds exhibit high purity and favorable stability, the extraction and purification processes have been optimized. Synthetic ORI-derived products exhibit anti-inflammatory and antibacterial activities, which are widely used as dietary supplements and functional beverages in daily life. Therefore, this paper reviews the source, extraction and purification, pharmacological effects, derivatives, content determination, toxicity and product applications of ORI. This has updated and deepened the understanding of ORI, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for its further research.

records.title: Cytotoxic metabolites from the endophytic fungus Aspergillus costaricensis y15
records.abstract: Eleven compounds (1–11), comprising two previously undescribed tetrahydrofuran derivatives (1–2) alongside nine recognized metabolites (3–11), were separated and purified from the EtOAc extract derived from the endophytic strain Aspergillus costaricensis. The structural determination of the compounds was achieved unambiguously through NMR spectroscopy, HRESIMS, and ECD analysis. Subsequent biological evaluation assessed the cytotoxic, antimicrobial, and α-glucosidase inhibitory properties of all isolates. Compound 10 exhibited moderate potency against the cancer cell lines MCF-7 and A549, with respective IC50 values of 22.0 ± 1.2 μM and 15.5 ± 1.1 μM. Overall, this investigation expands the chemical diversity of the genus Aspergillus and highlights compound 10 as a promising structural scaffold for further anticancer drug development.

records.title: A new acylated quercetin triglycoside with anti-inflammatory activity from the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida
records.abstract: Phytochemical investigation of the leaves of Camellia flavida var. flavida led to the isolation of a previously undescribed acylated quercetin triglycoside (1), together with three known constituents (2–4). Their structures were established by HR-ESI-MS with 1D and 2D NMR analyses and, for the known compounds, by comparison with reported spectroscopic data. Compound 1 was elucidated as quercetin 3-O-[β-D-glucopyranosyl-(1→3)]-[α-L-rhamnopyranosyl-(1→6)]-[2-O-(E)-p-coumaroyl]-β-D-glucopyranoside. Compounds 1–3 inhibited lipopolysaccharide-induced nitric oxide production in RAW 264.7 macrophages, with IC50 values of 14.9 ± 1.7, 13.4 ± 2.6, and 37.7 ± 2.9 μM, respectively, while their CC50 values were >64 μM. 4 was cytotoxic (CC50 10.9 ± 0.7 μM) and was therefore not evaluated for nitric oxide inhibition. These findings expand the known chemical diversity of C. flavida var. flavida and identify 1 and 2 as moderate inhibitors of nitric oxide production.

records.title: Gastroprotective potential of Bixa orellana: A critical review of extract-specific phytochemistry and preclinical evidence
records.abstract: Peptic ulcer disease remains clinically important despite effective Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) eradication and acid-suppressive therapy. Gastric injury reflects an imbalance between aggressive factors, including acid-pepsin activity, H. pylori, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), ethanol, oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and microvascular disturbance and protective mechanisms such as mucus-bicarbonate secretion, prostaglandin signaling, nitric oxide-regulated blood flow, epithelial restitution, and endogenous antioxidant defenses. Bixa orellana L. (annatto or achiote) is a tropical medicinal plant whose seed arils are rich in the apocarotenoids bixin and norbixin, whereas its leaves contain variable phenolics, flavonoids, tannins, terpenoids, alkaloids, and other constituents depending on geography, maturity, and extraction method. This critical narrative review uses a structured search and qualitative evidence-appraisal framework to evaluate extract-specific phytochemistry, direct gastric evidence, indirectly relevant gastrointestinal and vascular evidence, mechanistic plausibility, safety, quality control, and translational readiness. The available literature supports B. orellana as a biologically plausible preclinical mucosal-protective candidate, particularly for prevention of acute chemical injury; however, it does not establish clinical efficacy or chronic ulcer-healing activity. records.title: QUIMIOTERAPIA E MUCOSITE ORAL: AVALIAÇÃO DOS ESQUEMAS E CLASSIFICAÇÃO DAS LESÕES
records.abstract: Chemotherapy is widely used in the treatment of malignant neoplasms but is associated with significant adverse effects, such as oral mucositis (OM), which compromises patient’ quality of life. This review aims to analyze the main chemotherapy regimens associated with the occurrence of oral mucositis (OM), as well as the main agents involved in the development of lesions. This integrative review was conducted between March and May 2025, searching the PubMed, SciELO, and LILACS databases. Nine clinical studies were selected that analyzed different chemotherapy regimens and OM classifications according to the WHO, NCI-CTCAE, and JCOG scales. The highest incidence of OM was observed in protocols with antimetabolites (such as 5-FU and methotrexate), alkylating agents (such as melphalan), and monoclonal antibodies (such as panitumumab and cetuximab). The severity of the lesions varied according to the protocol, dosage, number of cycles, and clinical status of the patient. Therefore, the role of the dentist in the multidisciplinary oncology care team becomes essential for the prevention and effective management of OM during chemotherapy. Keywords: Oral Mucositis, Chemotherapy Protocols, Monoclonal Antibody.

records.title: Evolution of Food Science: Bridging Tradition and Innovation
records.journal: International Journal of Research and Review
records.abstract: Food science has evolved from indigenous culinary wisdom and ancient preservation methods into a complex interdisciplinary field that integrates modern technological advancements, systems biology, and data analytics. This transformation reflects a continuous interplay between traditional knowledge systems and cutting-edge scientific innovation aimed at addressing contemporary global challenges including nutrition security, public health, and environmental sustainability. This chapter comprehensively examines the historical foundations of food science, its scientific milestones, and contemporary innovations such as biotechnology, nanotechnology, and personalized nutrition. Further, it highlights integrative approaches that meld traditional practices with novel technologies, supported by illustrative case studies. Ethical considerations surrounding intellectual property and cultural stewardship are discussed alongside future directions emphasizing systems thinking, resilience, and equity. This synthesis articulates a pathway toward sustainable, ethical, and health-promoting food systems at the nexus of tradition and innovation. Keywords: food science, traditional knowledge, food innovation, biotechnology, functional foods, nutrigenomics, sustainability, food safety, culinary heritage

records.title: Nasal in-situ Transferosomes as a Platform Technology for Nose-to-Brain Drug Delivery
records.journal: Galore International Journal of Health Sciences and Research
records.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major obstacle in the therapeutic management of disorders related to the central nervous system (CNS), blocking the access of almost 98% of small molecule medications and practically all large molecules. Intranasal drug administration represents a viable alternative to overcome the BBB, based on its ability to deliver directly from the nasal cavities into the brain using the routes of olfactory and trigeminal nerves, offering a direct nose-to-brain drug delivery pathway. Despite its advantages, intranasal drug delivery remains constrained by factors such as quick clearance, short retention and poor permeation of the drugs through biological membranes, to address these challenges, the in-situ gelling systems containing mucoadhesive polymers have been developed. Nasal in-situ transferosomal gels offer a novel formulation technique that incorporates the benefits of both transferosomal vesicular drug delivery systems and stimuli-responsive gel matrices for brain targeting. Keywords: Transferosomes, in-situ gel, Intranasal, Nose-to-brain, Blood-brain barrier, Vesicular drug delivery, Mucoadhesive systems, Brain targeting.

records.title: Evaluating the Performance of Naïve Bayes and Support Vector Machine Classifiers for Diabetes Classification Using Cross-Validation
records.abstract: This study aims to compare the performance of the Naïve Bayes and Support Vector Machine algorithms in diabetes classification using the Pima Indians Diabetes Database. The dataset consists of 768 observations with eight predictor attributes and one target attribute, namely Outcome. The research methodology includes data understanding, preprocessing, model training, and evaluation using Stratified 10-Fold Cross-Validation. Preprocessing encompasses handling zero values on certain attributes, median imputation, and feature standardization for SVM. Evaluation was carried out using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and a confusion matrix. The test results showed that SVM obtained an average accuracy of 0.7474, precision of 0.6805, recall of 0.5373, F1-score of 0.5969, and ROC-AUC of 0.8256. Meanwhile, Naïve Bayes obtained an average accuracy of 0.7460, precision of 0.6610, recall of 0.6010, F1-score of 0.6222, and ROC-AUC of 0.8128. Based on the confusion matrix, Naïve Bayes correctly classified 161 of the 268 diabetes samples, whereas SVM correctly classified 144 samples. The results indicate that SVM achieved slightly higher accuracy and ROC-AUC, whereas Naïve Bayes provided better recall and F1-score values, demonstrating a superior capability in recognizing diabetes samples in this test. Consequently, algorithm selection must consider classification objectives and evaluation metrics, particularly when detecting the diabetes class is a priority.

records.journal: TEKNOSAINS Jurnal Sains Teknologi dan Informatika
records.abstract: Trading companies often face challenges in managing their inventory systems and finding it hard to match inventory levels with the increasing demand from consumers. This paper tries to create a system that can forecast how much of a product customers might want and also check how well different deep learning methods work. In this paper, the author uses both experimental and applied methods to check how well each deep learning algorithm works.The algorithms tested are CNN-LSTM, LSTM, GRU, BiLSTM, and Transformer. The author used data from Kaggle that includes 76,000 sales records from 2022 up to 2024, covering different product categories such as clothing, furniture, electronics, toys, and groceries. The data was then cleaned and split into groups for training and testing. The author found the results by testing various deep learning algorithms. The top performing algorithm is CNN-LSTM, which has MAE of 28.2136, RMSE of 36.6037, and R² of 0.3106. Even though the R2 value shows the model doesn't have strong predictive power yet, it is still the best performing model out of all the ones studied in this research. By comparing the system's performance to standard operating levels, it was found that the system can adjust to changes in demand.This suggests it could help trading companies better manage their stock and offer more understanding of how deep learning models work.

Contemporary evidence challenges this binary view, suggesting that transplant benefit depends less on diagnosis or anatomy alone than on careful candidate selection and disease behavior over time. records.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic inflammatory intestinal disorder affecting more than 7 million people worldwide, with a growing global burden. records.title: Bitter side of sweet: A stage-dependent immunometabolic model linking metabolic syndrome and inflammatory bowel disease
records.abstract: The increasing prevalence of metabolic syndrome (MetS) among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) has prompted renewed interest in their poorly defined bidirectional relationship, underpinned by shared mechanisms such as epithelial barrier disruption, chronic low-grade inflammation, and microbial dysbiosis. In this review, we comprehensively synthesize current evidence on the relationship between MetS and IBD, highlighting their shared pathophysiological mechanisms. We further propose a biphasic model of the MetS-IBD interaction, supported by original immunological data obtained from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and concomitant MetS. Early-stage MetS appears to promote a regulatory immune phenotype characterized by increased interleukin-10 and galectin-3-related pathways, which is associated with attenuated UC, whereas advanced MetS appears to be associated with a pro-inflammatory phenotype, increased interleukin-6 and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 signaling, cytotoxic immune-cell infiltration, mucosal damage, and more severe UC. This paradigm should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires validation in independent longitudinal cohorts. Nevertheless, it provides a translational framework for future biomarker development, metabolic stratification, and stage-adapted therapeutic research in patients with IBD and metabolic comorbidity.

records.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects over one-third of the global population, yet robust molecular biomarkers for early disease activity and treatment monitoring remain limited. Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) carry nucleic acids, proteins, and lipids that reflect disease-associated intercellular signaling and are being investigated as liquid-biopsy analytes and therapeutic platforms. Candidate sEV miRNAs, proteins, and lipid signatures have shown potential for disease characterization, but evidence derives mainly from small, heterogeneous cohorts with limited external validation. No sEV-based assay is established for routine MASLD diagnosis, staging, or treatment monitoring. Mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEVs and engineered sEV platforms have shown therapeutic potential in preclinical MASLD-related models through modulation of inflammation, oxidative stress, lipid metabolism, and targeted cargo delivery, although some engineering strategies remain supported primarily by non-MASLD proof-of-concept evidence. Key barriers to translation include heterogeneity in extracellular vesicle isolation and characterization, lipoprotein co-isolation, prospective multicenter validation, and, for therapeutic products, manufacturing consistency, biodistribution, dosing, and safety. This narrative review integrates diagnostic and therapeutic evidence within an evidence-classified translational framework.

records.title: Ameloblastic Carcinoma with Unusual Anterior Mandibular and Pharyngeal Extension in a Patient with Metachronous Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Case Report of a Complex Diagnostic Challenge
records.abstract: Ameloblastic carcinoma (AC) is a rare malignant odontogenic tumor characterized by aggressive local behavior and the potential for regional and distant metastasis. Anterior mandibular involvement with pharyngeal extension is exceptionally rare and poses significant diagnostic challenges. We report a 74‑year‑old man who presented with dysarthria, restricted tongue mobility, submental swelling, and intermittent intraoral bleeding. Imaging revealed an ill-defined radiolucent lesion in the anterior mandible with cortical destruction and extension into the oropharyngeal region. Incisional biopsy confirmed AC. Metastatic workup demonstrated bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy and multiple pulmonary nodules. A history of renal cell carcinoma (RCC), created diagnostic uncertainty regarding the origin of the distant lesions. The tumor was staged as T4bN2cM1 and deemed surgically unresectable. Palliative management was initiated; however, the patient died shortly thereafter. This case highlights a rare co-occurrence of atypical anatomical presentation and multi-malignancy diagnostic complexity, emphasizing the need for refined diagnostic strategies in similar scenarios.

records.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare perioperative outcomes after robotic-assisted vs. conventional laparoscopic total hysterectomy in frail women with endometrial cancer. METHODS: This retrospective study included female patients aged ≥50 years with endometrial cancer and frailty who received either robotic-assisted or conventional laparoscopic total hysterectomy, extracting data from the Nationwide Readmissions Database from 2016 to 2020. Outcomes included perioperative complications, length of stay (LOS), and 30- and 90-day readmission. Logistic and linear regression analyses were performed to compare outcomes between surgical approaches. RESULTS: In total, 1,212 patients with endometrial cancer and frailty were included. Robotic-assisted surgery was associated with significantly shorter LOS (adjusted beta=-0.34; 95% confidence interval [CI]=-0.46, -0.21; p<0.001), lower odds of sepsis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=0.57; 95% CI=0.34, 0.94; p=0.027) and surgical site infection (p=0.025), but higher odds of pneumonia (aOR=2.01; 95% CI=1.06, 3.84; p=0.033). CONCLUSION: Robotic-assisted hysterectomy in frail patients was associated with shorter LOS and fewer infection-related complications but a higher risk of pneumonia. Further studies are needed to optimize surgical decision-making in this population.

records.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Uterine cancer mortality is rising in the U.S. while other cancer deaths decline, posing a major public health challenge. High BMI is the strongest modifiable risk factor, but its full burden and associated inequalities remain poorly characterized. METHODS: Using data from Global Burden of Disease 2023 and National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES, 1999-2023), we assessed national and state-level trends in uterine cancer mortality (age-standardized mortality rate [ASMR]) and disability-adjusted life years (age-standardized disability-adjusted life year rate [ASDR]) from 1990-2023. We employed Joinpoint regression, frontier analysis, and AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average forecasting. records.title: Digital Twin Models for Cancer.
affiliations: Department of Biostatistics, China Pharmaceutical University, Nanjing, China.
records.abstract: The inherent complexity and heterogeneity of cancer create an urgent need for individualized treatment strategies. However, traditional population-based medical approaches have limitations in addressing patient-specific differences. Meanwhile, conventional clinical trials are often constrained by lengthy timelines, high costs, and difficulties in patient recruitment, particularly for rare cancers and pediatric populations, thereby hindering the development of novel therapies. To address these challenges, medical digital twins (MDTs) have emerged as dynamic computational models that represent an individual patient's physiology and disease state and are continuously updated as real-world data accumulate. To explain how MDTs transform accumulating patient data into actionable insights, this chapter first introduces their fundamental architecture, comprising five interdependent components: the patient, data connection, patient-in-silico, interface, and twin synchronization. Within this architecture, the patient-in-silico component can be constructed using mechanistic models based on established biological principles, artificial intelligence models driven by large-scale clinical data, or hybrid models combining both approaches. Representative mechanistic and artificial intelligence-driven MDTs are then presented to illustrate how these modeling approaches have been applied in oncology. Specifically, MDTs can support precision oncology and improve the efficiency of clinical trials.

Evidence was synthesized qualitatively and organized into organ-specific domains. records.title: Multiphoton Imaging of the Tibial Bone Marrow for In Vivo Spatial-Temporal Analysis of Myeloma Microenvironment and Treatment.
affiliations: Department of Pathology, Albert Einstein College of Medicine, Bronx, NY, USA. david.fooksman@einsteinmed.edu.
records.abstract: The bone marrow is a critical niche for multiple myeloma initiation, growth, and pathology. The biological and technical complexities of the bone marrow microenvironment make it challenging to study tumor physiology in situ. We have developed a thinned-bone surgical preparation for imaging the mouse tibial bone marrow. Using this approach, we have studied the spatial organization and temporal dynamics of myeloma cells, their interactions with the immune microenvironment, and the effects of acute drug treatments. In this chapter, we detail a protocol describing this procedure and present two use cases for intravital imaging to study dynamics tumors. In one study, we describe the use of photoactivation to capture live immune cells that are present within myeloma foci within the bone marrow for downstream analysis by flow cytometry or by other methods. In the second use case, we used imaging to capture effects of drug treatment in real-time in situ in the bone marrow to understand mechanisms of action and side effects.

records.title: Measurable Residual Disease.
affiliations: Department of Hematopathology, ACTREC, Tata Memorial Center, HBNI University, Room 18, CCE Building, ACTREC, Sector 22, Kharghar, Navi Mumbai, 410210, India. docprt@gmail.com.
records.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) serves as a critical biomarker of prognosis, treatment efficacy, and clinical outcome. It captures the presence of residual tumor cells below the detection threshold of conventional microscopy. Multiparametric flow cytometry (MFC) offers a rapid, cost-efficient, and widely applicable platform for MRD detection through leukemia-associated immunophenotypes (LAIPs) and deviation-from-normal (DfN) antigen maturation patterns. This technique underpins a wide range of clinical applications, including risk stratification, therapeutic decision-making, and post-transplant surveillance. This chapter outlines essential technical parameters for achieving high-sensitivity MRD detection across hematologic malignancies such as B-ALL, T-ALL, AML, MM, and CLL. Key topics covered include material required, reagent preparation, antibody panel design, sample processing and acquisition, gating strategies, and illustrative examples. Special emphasis is given to adaptations necessary for MRD monitoring following CD19-targeted therapies in B-ALL. By integrating rigorous methodology with evolving innovations, MFC continues to advance as a precise and expedient tool for MRD assessment, contributing significantly to personalized treatment strategies.

records.title: Metabolic Reprogramming and Tumor Microenvironment: Emerging Mechanisms of Cancer Development and Therapeutic Resistance
records.abstract: Cancer progression is driven by complex interactions between metabolic reprogramming, mitochondrial dysfunction, and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Cancer cells undergo profound metabolic adaptations that enable them to sustain rapid proliferation, maintain redox balance, and survive under conditions of hypoxia, nutrient deprivation, and cellular stress. Although aerobic glycolysis is a recognized feature of many tumors, mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) remains essential in numerous cancer types, contributing to ATP production, biosynthetic pathways, and metabolic flexibility. These complementary energy-generating mechanisms allow malignant cells to adapt to changing microenvironmental conditions and maintain tumor growth.The tumor microenvironment further shapes cancer metabolism through interactions among malignant cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts, immune cells, endothelial cells, and extracellular matrix components. Hypoxia-inducible signaling, nutrient competition, lactate accumulation, and altered lipid and amino acid metabolism can promote angiogenesis, immune evasion, invasion, and metastatic dissemination. In addition, metabolic communication between tumor cells and surrounding stromal cells can influence mitochondrial activity, inflammatory signaling, and resistance to anticancer treatments. records.title: DISSEMINATED, FATAL TRICHOSPORON ASAHII FUNGAEMIA IN A CRITICALLY ILL COVID-19 PATIENT: A CASE REPORT AND REVIEW OF THE LITERATURE
records.journal: Journal of Defence Science Engineering & Technology
records.abstract: The usage of immunomodulators and immunosuppressants in critically ill COVID-19 patients increase the risk for opportunistic infections such as fungaemia. Trichosporon asahii is a yeast-like basidiomycete normally found in soil, plants, and birds that could cause rare, invasive trichosporonosis in immunocompromised patients. A 74-year-old man with comorbid dyslipidaemia and hypertension who completed two doses of COVID-19 vaccination was initially admitted for ascending cholangitis. He was infected with COVID-19 on the sixth day of admission and deteriorated, which required intubation with intensive care, and started on high-dose steroids as well as immunomodulators. However, he developed a multidrug-resistant nosocomial infection with T. asahii fungaemia. Antifungals fluconazole and voriconazole were started, while the steroid was tapered down. The patient succumbed to multiple organ dysfunction and acute respiratory distress syndrome despite aggressive management in the ICU. Fungaemia by T. asahii is a threat to critically ill COVID-19 patients despite treatment with antifungal agents proven to be effective, which warrants further research for more refined management guidelines and to identify alternative therapies to improve patients’ survival.

records.title: Majority Filter For Enhancing Pixel-Based Random Forest Land Cover Classification In Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency
records.abstract: High-quality land cover data are essential for environmental policy, spatial planning, and ecosystem monitoring. However, pixel-based classification methods, while widely used due to their practicality, often suffer from salt-and-pepper noise, which undermines map reliability. This study aimed to integrate Random Forest (RF) classification and majority filtering to enhance the quality of land cover mapping in Sukajaya District, Bogor Regency. RF was applied to Sentinel-2 image data with varying numbers of trees (ntree) to determine the optimal model performance. Subsequently, majority filtering was applied to each classification result to reduce noise and improve spatial coherence. The evaluation employed multiple accuracy metrics, including User’s Accuracy (UA), Producer’s Accuracy (PA), F1-Score, Overall Accuracy (OA), and Kappa Coefficient (KC). Comprehensive accuracy increased with the ntree until reaching an optimal point. Beyond this point, additional ntree resulted in diminishing returns. Applying majority filtering as a post-processing procedure led to further improvements in classification accuracy. While majority filtering can reduce classification noise and improve the visual quality of land cover maps, it also carries the risk of removing small, accurately classified land cover patches. This consequence is rarely discussed in similar studies. These findings highlight the importance of integrating pixel-based machine learning classification with majority filtering

records.title: THE PRECISION APPROACH IN CONTEMPORARY NEUROSURGICAL PRACTICE: A REVIEW
affiliations: Russian Medical Academy of Continuous Professional Education
records.journal: Problems of Social Hygiene Public Health and History of Medicine
records.abstract: The review was based on analysis of 180 sources from databases PubMed, eLibrary, Cohrane Library, MEDLINE for 2015-2025 using keywords precision medicine, personalized medicine, neuro-oncology, oncology, cranio-cerebral injury, neuro-trauma, neuro-proteomics and AI. The purpose of the study was to demonstrate, on the basis of analysis of publications on precision medicine application in neurosurgery, the significance and perspectives of mentioned approach in modern neurosurgical practice. The methods of precision medicine, digital revolution and progress in multi-modal Big Data processing permit to better understand of tumor genesis, their clinical heterogeneity, functional effects and causes underlying their resistance to treatment. The precision medicine methods provide valuable information on pathophysiological mechanisms underlying neuro-trauma through analysis of complex protein interactions and changes. The future of precision medicine in neurosurgical practice is in permanent enhancement of AI and machine learning, permitting rapid and accurate decision-making based on comprehensive molecular data. The future of neurosurgery lies in harmonious integration of such interdisciplinary approaches as precision medicine and clinical neurosurgery to discover new possibilities of targeted and personalized therapy.

records.title: Tumor-treating fields in gastrointestinal cancers: Mechanisms, clinical evidence, and emerging precision therapy
records.abstract: Tumor-treating fields (TTFields) are low-intensity, intermediate-frequency alternating electric fields that convert physical energy into biological stress within dividing cancer cells. Initially recognized for their ability to disrupt mitosis, TTFields are now understood to influence a broader range of cancer-related processes, including DNA replication, repair pathways, cellular organization, and immunogenic cell death. These mechanisms are particularly relevant to gastrointestinal malignancies, where deep anatomy, stromal barriers, organ motion, peritoneal dissemination, and cumulative systemic toxicity limit conventional treatment escalation. Pancreatic cancer is currently the leading gastrointestinal indication for TTFields. In the PANOVA-3 trial, TTFields combined with standard chemotherapy improved overall survival without additional systemic toxicity, although tumor shrinkage and conventional progression-free survival remained unchanged. Evidence in hepatocellular, gastric, biliary tract, and colorectal cancers remains preliminary and should be interpreted as mechanistic or hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing. This article argues that TTFields should not be understood as a simple on-or-off device exposure. records.title: Metabolic commonalities in colorectal and gastric cancer: Taurine metabolism as a key regulatory node and its translational implications
affiliations: Dongzhimen Hospital Affiliated to Beijing University of Chinese Medicine
records.abstract: As the two most frequently occurring digestive system cancers, colorectal cancer and gastric cancer share many commonalities in terms of their epidemiology, metabolic reprogramming and microenvironmental regulation. Recent studies have demonstrated that dysregulated taurine metabolism is an important hub in the metabolic network of both cancers, contributing to tumor progression via several mechanisms, including modulation of energy metabolism, remodeling of the immune microenvironment, interaction with gut microbiota, and maintenance of oxidative stress balance. The aberrant features of taurine metabolism and the molecular mechanisms in colorectal cancer and gastric cancer were systematically discussed, the central role of taurine metabolism in tumor metabolic reprogramming, immune evasion and inflammation-cancer transformation was discussed in detail, and the clinical translational prospects of targeting taurine metabolism as a potential diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target were outlined, which provides new theoretical foundations and strategic insights for the precise prevention and treatment of both cancers.

records.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps in gastrointestinal malignancies: Friend or foe?
records.abstract: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), chromatin-based webs released by activated neutrophils, were first described as antimicrobial scaffolds, but these structures now appear in sterile inflammation, thrombosis, and cancer. In gastrointestinal malignancies, experimental and clinical studies have connected NETs with tumor growth, immune escape, cancer-associated thrombosis, postoperative recurrence, and metastatic spread. NET-derived DNA, histones, neutrophil elastase, myeloperoxidase, and citrullinated histones can remodel the tumor microenvironment, shield tumor cells from cytotoxic lymphocytes, promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition, awaken dormant cells, and help metastatic cells colonize distant organs. However, NETs are not simply harmful. They remain part of host defense and may restrain tumor cells in selected inflammatory, infectious, or treatment-related settings. This review summarizes NET biology in colorectal, gastric, hepatocellular, pancreatic, and other gastrointestinal cancers, focusing on the therapies that inhibit NET formation, degrade NET scaffolds, or block NET-tumor cell interactions.

records.title: Extracellular vesicles in gastrointestinal diseases: A narrative minireview of translational readiness
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) mediate communication among epithelial, immune, stromal, microbial, and tumor compartments in gastrointestinal diseases. This narrative minireview integrates inflammatory bowel disease and major gastrointestinal malignancies (colorectal, gastric, pancreatic, and liver cancers) using a five-stage translational-readiness framework: Discovery, analytical validation, clinical validation, regulatory development, and implementation. We distinguish discovery-stage and preclinical findings from clinically validated applications. EV cargo and engineered EV platforms show potential for biomarker panels, liquid biopsy, drug delivery, and regenerative medicine, but no broad EV assay or therapeutic platform is established for routine precision gastroenterology. Key barriers include pre-analytical variability, isolation-dependent results, incomplete cargo attribution, cohort heterogeneity, limited independent validation, and manufacturing and safety requirements. Progress will require standardized workflows, disease-specific comparators, prospective multicenter validation, and evidence-calibrated integration of EV data with conventional biomarkers and multi-omics.

records.title: Helicobacter pylori status in gastric cancer immunotherapy: Conflicting clinical associations, immune-microbial mechanisms, and biomarker challenges
affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China
records.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have become an important treatment option for gastric cancer, but therapeutic responses remain highly heterogeneous. Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori ), a major risk factor for gastric carcinogenesis, may continue to influence tumor immunity and immunotherapy outcomes after cancer develops. However, current clinical findings are inconsistent, and the biomarker value of H. pylori remains uncertain. This review critically summarizes the clinical and mechanistic evidence linking H. pylori status to ICI outcomes in gastric cancer. Potential mechanisms include regulation of programmed cell death protein 1/programmed death-ligand 1 signaling, T-cell function, antigen presentation, myeloid immunosuppression, and microbial ecology. The divergent clinical results may reflect differences in infection status, detection methods, tumor molecular subtypes, disease stage, treatment setting, and previous therapeutic exposures. Current evidence does not support H. pylori as a validated predictive biomarker for ICI response. Rather, it may represent a context-dependent indicator of the tumor-immune-microbial background. Prospective longitudinal studies with standardized definitions of current active infection, previous infection of uncertain current status, successfully eradicated infection, and no evidence of previous infection are needed to determine whether specific H. pylori -related biological states modify the relative benefit of immunotherapy.

records.title: Sporadic diffuse gastric cancer in Western populations and the mismatch between tumour biology and clinical care
records.abstract: The epidemiology of gastric cancer is changing in Western populations. Population growth and ageing are projected to increase absolute case numbers despite declining age-standardised incidence, while historical registry data suggest changes in the relative contribution of diffuse-type disease, subject to period and coding effects. These trends give renewed urgency to understanding a cancer whose biology challenges established care. This narrative minireview examines the resulting gaps in prevention, diagnosis, staging and treatment of sporadic diffuse-type gastric cancer. No validated precursor sequence supports subtype-specific surveillance, and infiltrative growth complicates detection. Treatment presents a further mismatch: Enrichment for genomically stable biology and lower frequencies of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 positivity and mismatch-repair deficiency restrict some therapeutic opportunities, while variable programmed death-ligand 1 expression requires individual assessment. Systemic trials have transformed gastric cancer care, but their heterogeneous populations and exploratory histological analyses leave diffuse-specific benefit incompletely defined. records.title: Tumor-associated macrophages in gastric cancer: Phenotypic plasticity and therapeutic targets
affiliations: China Academy of Chinese Medical Sciences
records.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are abundant, functionally plastic cells within the gastric cancer tumor microenvironment and influence tumor growth, invasion, metastasis, angiogenesis, immune evasion, chemoresistance, and metabolic reprogramming. The M1/M2 dichotomy incompletely describes TAM states; single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies have identified specialized populations that vary with tumor subtype, anatomical niche, and disease stage. This review synthesizes current evidence on TAM origin, recruitment, adaptation, and roles in malignant progression, and examines TAM-directed therapeutic strategies. TAM composition and polarization, rather than total macrophage density, may be more relevant to treatment response. Although TAM-targeting approaches show promise in preclinical models, direct clinical targeting in gastric cancer remains limited. Defining subtype-specific TAM states, clarifying microbiota-TAM interactions, and developing predictive biomarkers may advance precision immunotherapy.

records.title: SSDHR classifier network for brain tumor detection using MRI images
records.journal: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology (IJ-ICT)
records.abstract: Brain tumors are the chaotic growth of abnormal brain cells, which is the main cause of cancer worldwide. Symptoms vary depending on tumor size and location, and these tumors can be cancerous or non-cancerous. Early detection and characterization are crucial but challenging due to the brain's complex structure. This study proposes a self-supervised classification deep hierarchical reconstruction network (SSDHR), a combination of generative and discriminative models. This network uses convolutional Kernels of different sizes for processing of input data on separate branches to extract effective discriminative features. A parallel-structured symmetric fusion attention (SFA) module is introduced, combining attention mechanisms for coordinates, time, and frequency to enhance the model's comprehension and feature selection. The SSDHR classifier network achieves the highest accuracy (91.9%) among 10 state-of-the-art classifiers, classifying tumors into 4 classes: pituitary, meningioma, glioma, and no tumor. The model's performance is evaluated using various metrics that demonstrate its effectiveness in brain tumor classification.

records.title: Sequential Mitochondrial Transplantation Abrogates Agmatine-Mediated Neuroprotection Against 6-OHDA Toxicity in SH-SY5Y Cells
records.abstract: Objective: Parkinson disease (PD) involves dopaminergic neuron loss from mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress. We investigated the combined, sequential effects of mesenchymal stem cell–derived mitochondrial transplantation (MitoTr) and pharmacological agmatine modulation in a PD–like undifferentiated SH-SY5Y cellular model. Methods: Undifferentiated SH-SY5Y cells were exposed to 6-hydroxydopamine (6-OHDA; 350 μM) for 24 hours and sequentially treated with mitochondria (5 or 10 μg/mL) and agmatine (100 μM; 2 hours post-MitoTr). Cell viability was assessed via MTT assays (n = 8 independent experiments). Total-lysate cytochrome c ELISA (n = 3) and Western blots for DJ-1, REDD1, and α-synuclein (n = 4) were performed across 4 core groups. Results: 6-OHDA significantly reduced viability compared with Control (mean [SEM], 0.50 [0.05] vs 1.00 [0.04]; P < .001); postinjury agmatine restored it to near-control levels (mean [SEM], 0.97 [0.20]; P < .001\) vs 6-OHDA), while agmatine alone had no effect (P > .99). Conversely, MitoTr-containing groups showed significantly lower viability than Control, Agmatine, and Agmatine + 6-OHDA groups (P < .001). records.title: Breast cancer screening in Europe and the role of general practitioners: A 32-country comparative survey.
records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: Introduction Breast cancer is the commonest cancer in women, and screening can allow earlier-stage diagnosis. While there are European recommendations on the age-range and frequency of breast cancer screening, participation in these programmes varies substantially, and this could be due to differences in how they are organised and implemented. The role that primary healthcare professionals play in the process is unclear.We aimed to describe the breast cancer screening programmes in European countries and investigate how primary healthcare professionals are involved in this screening process.Methods A cross-sectional survey in 32 countries. Key informants with relevant expertise answered online questions about the characteristics of their screening programmes and general practitioners' (GPs') roles in this. Responses were refined through an iterative consensus process. Data were examined to identify patterns in GP engagement.Results We found important differences between European breast cancer screening systems. While most had population-based screening, four countries relied on opportunistic screening. In 15 countries GPs had little or no involvement in the process of breast cancer screening, and in 13 countries GPs had some involvement, including identifying eligible patients, issuing referrals, and following-up results. Screening uptake rates tended to be higher in countries with well-established population-based screening programmes which give little or no GP involvement.

affiliations: University of West Bohemia in Pilsen
records.journal: ASEAN Journal for Science and Engineering in Materials
records.abstract: This review evaluates the application of deep learning (DL) for the predictive modeling of electronic materials in computer engineering. We analyzed peer-reviewed literature across four major databases, focusing exclusively on advanced architectures like Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Generative models. Results indicate these models accurately predict critical properties, such as band gaps and thermal conductivity, for next-generation semiconductors, 2D materials, and memristors. These high accuracies are achieved because architectures like GNNs effectively capture complex 3D spatial interactions without requiring manual feature engineering. However, practical fabrication remains hindered by data scarcity, algorithmic opacity, and a profound "Sim-to-Real Gap". While DL accelerates predictive design, sustaining Moore's Law ultimately requires developing autonomous "Self-Driving Labs" and Large Material Models to bridge digital predictions with physical synthesis.

records.journal: Open Access CRIS of the University of Bern
records.abstract: AIMS: Tumour budding (TB) has been recognized as an additional prognostic factor in the TNM (2017) and WHO (2019) classification systems. However, its prognostic impact in stages II and III colorectal cancer (CRC) remains inconsistently defined. This study aims to systematically evaluate the prognostic value of high-grade TB in stage II-III CRC. Subgroup analysis stratified by TNM stage revealed that high-grade TB consistently predicted adverse outcomes in both stage II and stage III disease. records.abstract: The glycocalyx is a carbohydrate-rich layer formed by glycoproteins, glycolipids, proteoglycans, and glycosaminoglycans at the outer cell surface. These changes affect how tumor cells sense force, bind the extracellular matrix, cluster receptors, evade immune surveillance, survive in circulation, and arrest at distant vascular beds. Meanwhile, pathology, imaging, glycoproteomics, and liquid-biopsy studies have started to define glycocalyx-derived biomarkers with diagnostic and prognostic value, especially in hepatocellular carcinoma, pancreatic cancer, breast cancer, and hematologic malignancies. This review summarizes the structure of the cancer glycocalyx, the molecular programs that remodel it, and the consequences of these changes for tumor progression. records.title: Triage models for surgical decision-making in patients with shoulder pain: an integrative review.
records.abstract: Shoulder pain is a major cause of work absenteeism, affecting 1 in 3 adults. Although nonsurgical treatments like physical therapy are recommended as the first line of management, 40% of patients are referred for surgery before exploring these options. This review aimed to identify existing triage models used for shoulder pain referrals for surgery, guidelines for shoulder pain management that include criteria for surgical referral, and indications for surgery. An integrative review approach was used to comprehensively search major databases (Medline, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL Plus) and gray literature. Articles on triage models, referral processes, or surgery candidacy for shoulder pain were included. The searches retrieved 4510 articles, with 480 selected for full review and 71 articles included in this synthesis. Thirty-seven articles described various triage models and clinical decision-making processes for managing shoulder pain, including determining when to refer for surgical consultation and the indications for surgery. Seventeen articles compared surgical and nonsurgical treatments to identify surgical indicators, 10 articles examined factors affecting decision-making, and 7 articles explored predictor models for surgical outcomes. The findings underscore the need for a multifactorial decision-making process that acknowledges the complexity of pain within a biopsychosocial framework and incorporates patients' personal preferences into the triage decision-making process.

records.abstract: Medical cannabis, also known as medical marijuana, is becoming a more popular treatment for many diseases, including chronic pain. Chronic pain is difficult to treat, and current pain relievers are less effective in women. Medical cannabis may be a useful alternative to the medications that are currently available, but more research is needed to determine how safe and effective it is. Cannabis belongs to a class of drugs known as cannabinoids, which act on the body’s own endocannabinoid system to produce its effects. Cannabinoids affect the sexes differently, but it is not clear what causes these differences. Our research explored how sex hormones like estrogen and testosterone affect the efficacy of cannabinoids. To do this, I first examined whether removing these hormones would affect the brain’s response to THC, the main ingredient in cannabis. I found that THC affected brain regions differently in mice with depleted hormones. Additionally, THC affected brain regions differently in males and females. Next, I tested whether testosterone and estrogen affected how well cannabinoids worked as pain relievers. I found that testosterone reduced the drug’s efficacy in females, while estrogens reduced its efficacy in males. This would suggest that hormones have a different effect on males and females, leading to differences in the cannabinoid’s pain-relieving ability. records.title: Thiolutin alleviates acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) in a mouse model of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
affiliations: Beijing Institute of Microbiology and Epidemiology
records.abstract: Acute graft-versus-host disease (aGVHD) is a major, life-threatening complication in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), and the development of novel molecular-targeted therapies for aGVHD is urgently needed. Thiolutin (THL), a disulfide-containing antibiotic, inhibits the activity of the BRCC3-containing isopeptidase complex and thereby suppresses NLR pyrin domain-containing protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation. Here, we investigated the effect of THL on aGVHD in a mouse model of allo-HSCT. We found that THL significantly improved survival in aGVHD recipients, reduced weight loss and clinical scores, and attenuated pathological changes in aGVHD target organs, including the liver, small intestine, and colon. Furthermore, THL diminished donor T-cell activation and infiltration into target organs and promoted the expansion of regulatory T cells. THL also inhibited NLRP3 inflammasome activation and reduced the production of proinflammatory cytokines, including tumor necrosis factor (TNF), interferon γ (IFN-γ), interleukin (IL)-2, IL-17A, and IL-1β. This study reveals a previously unrecognized role of THL in regulating aGVHD and highlights its potential as an anti-inflammatory therapeutic agent for clinical development in patients undergoing allo-HSCT.

The first part of the study examined usual nutrient intake and micronutrient adequacy. Overall micronutrient adequacy was high at 96%. However, important dietary concerns remained. Many adolescents had low intakes of calcium and magnesium and consumed high amounts of saturated fat, added sugars, and sodium. Ultra-processed foods contributed about two-thirds of total daily energy intake, with differences observed across demographic groups. records.abstract: The digital-aided support is still basically patient-focused, generic in terms of sentiment coverage, and not linked to real-time emotional condition, although the psychological load on a caregiver of brain tumor patients often exceeds the levels in caregivers of other types of cancer. A pilot experiment conducted on annotated social media data with a lexicon-based rule and three machine-learning classifiers (Naive Bayes, Support Vector machine and Logistic Regression) was conducted to test the basic role-classification feature of the system that classifies text written by caregivers and that by patients. records.title: Non-cirrhotic hyperammonemia in adults: Recognition and management
records.abstract: In adults, an elevated ammonia level is almost reflexively attributed to cirrhosis. Yet hyperammonemia also occurs in patients with structurally normal livers, in whom the underlying cause is often missed. This delay matters because hyperammonemic brain injury depends on both the magnitude and duration of ammonia elevation. This review organizes the non-cirrhotic causes by mechanism. Ammonia production increases with urease-producing urinary tract infections, Ureaplasma or Mycoplasma infection after lung transplantation, heavy nitrogen loads, malignancy and chemotherapy, and urinary diversion. Clearance is impaired in adult-onset urea cycle disorders, with drugs such as valproate, post-gastric bypass, and when portal blood bypasses the liver through a portosystemic shunt. We outline a practical diagnostic approach: Confirm a true elevation using a properly handled sample, exclude cirrhosis, then use targeted testing, including plasma amino acids, urine orotic acid, acid-base assessment, acylcarnitine and zinc levels, and Doppler or cross-sectional imaging, to distinguish among these mechanisms. Management proceeds on two tracks: Lowering ammonia while simultaneously treating the underlying cause, which can be curative in several conditions. Early measurement of ammonia in patients with unexplained encephalopathy and normal liver tests can prevent avoidable neurologic injury.

records.title: Nuclear factor I connects H3K27M to a targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma
records.abstract: Diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma is a lethal pediatric brainstem cancer with few effective treatments. Here, we integrate metabolomic, transcriptomic, chromatin, genetic and in vivo analyses to identify a purine-metabolic dependency associated with the H3K27M histone mutation. The histone H3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitution increases Nuclear Factor I transcriptional activity, which promotes coordinated expression of enzymes involved in purine biosynthesis and degradation, including 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase/inosine monophosphate cyclohydrolase and purine nucleoside phosphorylase. Sustained purine degradation limits feedback inhibition of purine synthesis, enabling continued purine production, utilization and catabolism. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of the terminal de novo purine biosynthesis enzyme reduces tumor-cell fitness, slows orthotopic tumor progression and extends survival in mice. These results connect histone-mutation-associated chromatin remodeling to a Nuclear Factor I-regulated, therapeutically targetable purine dependency in diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma.

records.title: Exploration of phospholipid metabolism-related prognostic genes and construction of a risk model in endometrial cancer based on transcriptomics
records.abstract: Dysregulated phospholipid metabolism is implicated in endometrial cancer (EC) progression, but the prognostic relevance of phospholipid metabolism-related genes (PMRGs) remains unclear. This study identified prognostic PMRGs and constructed a risk-stratification model for EC. EC transcriptome datasets and PMRGs were obtained from public databases. Prognostic genes were screened through differential expression analysis and LASSO-Cox regression, and a risk score classified patients into high- (HRG) and low-risk (LRG) groups. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), immune infiltration, and drug sensitivity analyses were performed to explore underlying mechanisms, and RT-qPCR validated candidate genes. A three-gene signature (SPATA18, XBP1, LPCAT1) showed favorable prognostic performance. Pathways including Fatty Acid Metabolism, cell adhesion molecules, and cardiac muscle contraction were differentially enriched between groups (p < 0.05). SPATA18 correlated positively with eosinophils (cor = 0.35) and negatively with effector memory CD4⁺ T cells (cor = − 0.41). IC50 values of 170 drugs, including Dactolisib, Afuresertib, and Uprosertib, differed significantly between groups (p < 0.05). RT-qPCR confirmed XBP1 up-regulation and SPATA18 down-regulation in EC (p < 0.05). This phospholipid metabolism-based signature, integrating metabolic and immune features, provides a framework for risk stratification and personalized treatment in EC.

records.abstract: T cell recognition of specific antigens presented by major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) can play an important role during immune responses against pathogens and cancer cells. Detection of T cell immunity is based on assessing the presence of antigen-specific cytotoxic CD8+ T cells using MHC-I multimer technology. Previously, we have designed conditional peptides for HLA-A*02:01, H-2K b, and HLA-E that form stable peptide-MHC-I-complexes at low temperatures and dissociate when exposed to a defined elevated temperature. The resulting conditional MHC-I complex can easily and without additional handling be exchanged with a peptide of interest, allowing to exchange peptides in a ready-to-use multimer and a high-throughput manner. Here, we present data that this peptide-exchange technology is a generally applicable, ready-to-use, and fast approach to load many different peptides in MHC-I multimers for alleles of the HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C loci. We describe the development of conditional peptides for HLA-A*03:01, HLA-A*11:01, HLA-B*07:02, and HLA-C*07:02 that only form stable peptide-MHC-I complexes at low temperatures, allowing peptide exchange at higher defined temperatures. We document the ease and flexibility of this technology by monitoring CD8+T cell responses to virus-specific peptide-MHC complexes in patients.

records.title: Central nervous system aspergillosis with negative serum fungal biomarkers after sequential teclistamab and talquetamab for multiple myeloma: a case report and review of the literature
affiliations: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland
records.abstract: Bispecific antibodies directed against B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) and G protein-coupled receptor class C group 5 member D (GPRC5D) have improved outcomes in relapsed multiple myeloma but are associated with a high burden of infection. Invasive mould infection of the central nervous system (CNS) has rarely been described in this setting. We report a 70-year-old woman with heavily pretreated IgG-kappa myeloma who received teclistamab, complicated by immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) treated with corticosteroids, followed by talquetamab. She received antiviral and anti- Pneumocystis prophylaxis and intravenous immunoglobulin, without mould-active cover. Shortly after starting talquetamab, she developed cough and confusion, with cavitating pulmonary lesions initially attributed to bacterial abscesses. Serum galactomannan remained 0.1 on serial testing and β-D-glucan was negative. Computed tomography-guided lung biopsy confirmed pulmonary aspergillosis, and voriconazole was started. Failure to regain her functional baseline and progressive weakness, initially difficult to separate from her previous ICANS, led to brain magnetic resonance imaging, which showed a 10-mm ring-enhancing occipital lesion. Biopsy confirmed CNS aspergillosis. A literature review identified few published cases of invasive aspergillosis during bispecific therapy for myeloma, and serum galactomannan was positive in those with reported results. records.title: Analytical platform for mRNA quantification using RNAscope and fluorescent melamine nanoparticles
records.abstract: hybridisation (ISH) is widely used for detecting mRNA and enables efficient spatially resolved analysis of gene expression in cells and tissues. However, conventional chromogenic and fluorescent detection methods often exhibit limited reproducibility and photostability, undermining reliable quantification and longitudinal studies. To address these limitations, we developed a novel analytical approach combining RNAscope with fluorescent-dye-loaded melamine nanoparticles, referred to as phosphor-integrated dots (PIDs), for the precise, quantitative visualisation of epidermal growth factor receptor, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 and human epidermal growth factor receptor 3 mRNAs in formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded samples from seven cancer cell lines spanning a wide expression range. This PID-based RNA ISH method generated objective, highly quantitative signals without enzymatic amplification, thereby overcoming the constraints of traditional staining approaches. Furthermore, by preserving spatial context and supporting robust quantification, it enabled detailed assessment of tumour heterogeneity and facilitated the detection of rare cell populations. records.title: Construction of a Habitat Analysis-Integrated Radiomics Model to Predict KRAS Mutation Status and risk stratification in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
affiliations: Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University
Third Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University
records.abstract: Objectives To explore the predictive performance of a habitat analysis-integrated radiomics model for identifying KRAS mutation status and supporting individualized risk stratification in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Methods This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 359 patients with pathologically confirmed NSCLC from two independent medical centers. Three predictive models were built: a clinical-feature-based model, a conventional whole-tumor radiomics model, and a habitat analysis-integrated radiomics model. All CT images were processed using a standardized preprocessing pipeline. Three machine-learning algorithms, including support-vector machines, random forests, and ExtraTrees classifiers, were applied for model training and optimization. Model discriminative performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed to quantify the clinical net benefit. An individualized risk-prediction nomogram was constructed based on the optimal multi-feature fusion model. Results Among all models, the habitat analysis-integrated radiomics model demonstrated the best predictive capability.Habitat-derived features and fused multidimensional features yielded significantly higher AUC values than clinical features alone or conventional whole-tumor radiomic features, indicating superior capacity to capture intratumoral heterogeneity. records.title: Trial architecture in contemporary cardio-oncology: Why parallel-group randomized controlled trials may not fit every cardiotoxicity phenotype
records.abstract: Cardio-oncology has evolved rapidly with immune checkpoint inhibitors, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies, and targeted kinase inhibitors, yet cardiovascular prevention strategies remain largely informed by evidence generated during the anthracycline era. This critical narrative review examines why cardioprotection trials have failed to keep pace with these evolving toxicity mechanisms, analyzing trial populations, endpoint selection, biomarker strategies, imaging approaches, and overall trial design across traditional and newer cancer therapies, rather than summarizing therapeutic efficacy. The evidence shows a persistent mismatch between contemporary toxicity phenotypes and existing trial design: Most studies continue to focus on anthracycline-associated left ventricular dysfunction and surrogate imaging endpoints, while immune-mediated myocarditis, cytokine release syndrome-related cardiomyopathy, vascular toxicities, arrhythmias, and other emerging phenotypes remain inadequately represented, compounded by limited biological stratification, one-size-fits-all prevention strategies, heterogeneous outcome definitions, and insufficient mechanism-specific monitoring. Progress in cardio-oncology prevention is constrained not only by the availability of candidate cardioprotective interventions but by the near-uniform persistence of a single trial architecture across mechanistically distinct toxicities. records.title: Underwater Endoscopic Mucosal Resection for Serrated Lesions: A Systematic Review and Single-Arm Meta-Analysis.
affiliations: Gastroenterology Department Universidade Federal de São Paulo (UNIFESP) São Paulo Brazil.
records.abstract: Background and aims Sessile serrated lesions (SSLs) are established colorectal cancer precursors, and complete removal is essential. Although underwater endoscopic mucosal resection (UEMR) has gained acceptance for nonpedunculated colorectal lesions, evidence specific to SSLs remains limited. We conducted a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis to evaluate the efficacy and safety of UEMR for SSLs. Methods PubMed, EMBASE, and Cochrane databases were searched through June 2025 for studies reporting UEMR outcomes in SSLs. The primary outcome was R0 resection. Secondary outcomes included en bloc resection, complete resection, recurrence, and adverse events (AEs). Pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was assessed with I 2 . Results Seven observational studies including 581 lesions were analyzed. Median lesion size ranged from 12 to 24.6 mm. R0 resection was achieved in 72.5% (95% CI, 58.4-83.2), decreasing to 63.6% for lesions ≥10 mm. The pooled complete resection rate was 90.5% (95% CI, 69.6-100) en bloc resection rate was 80.4% (95% CI, 65.0-90.1). AEs were uncommon, with a pooled incidence of 0.56% (95% CI, 0-1.74), including six delayed bleeding events and five perforations. Recurrence was assessed in three studies (with a pooled rate of 2.37% (95% CI, 1.24-4.49; I 2 = 0%). records.title: Interleukin-6 induces epithelial-mesenchymal transition in breast cancer cells
affiliations: Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Médicas y Nutrición Salvador Zubirán
records.abstract: Background: Breast cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related death in Mexico, with most deaths being related to locally advanced or metastatic disease at diagnosis.Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is one of the steps that are indispensable for metastasis.Different factors trigger EMT, like TGF-β, EGF and interleukin 6 (IL-6), among others.EMT is characterized by E-cadherin expression loss and N-cadherin and vimentin expression.In this study, we investigated the role of IL-6 on EMT induction.Methods: MBCDF and MBCD17 primary breast cancer cell cultures were used.E-cadherin expression was measured by Western Blot.Cells were stimulated with IL-6 to induce EMT.STAT3 activation was measured using phospho-specific antibodies, and E-cadherin expression was measured as EMT marker.Results: MBCDF and MBCD17 primary breast cancer cell cultures stimulation with IL-6 induced STAT3-Tyr705 phosphorylation without its total levels being altered; in addition, IL-6 cell-stimulation was shown to induce EMT, as evidenced by E-cadherin loss.Conclusions: The results of the present work suggest that IL-6 induces EMT in primary breast cancer cell cultures through STAT3 phosphorylation.(creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
